question: Under United States copyright law, who is deemed the author of a work made "for hire"?

question: In the Family Guy segment "High School History," which city does Harry Truman nuke after misreading FDR's order to make peace with Japan?

question: In the Family Guy episode "A House Full of Peters," a clone says it was "Orphan Blacked." Which TV series does that line reference?
reply: It's a nod to Orphan Black, the series about a young con artist who finds out she's one of many clones. The episode also borrows from the show when Meg's clone pretends to be her by copying her accent and mannerisms, the way the clones on Orphan Black often impersonate each other.
source: The clone’s line about being “Orphan Blacked” is a reference to the series Orphan Black where a young con artist finds out she is one of many clones, right down to Meg’s clone impersonating her and copying her accent and mannerisms as many occasions on the show the clones impersonate one another using disguises and change their voices.

question: In Family Guy, when Peter tries to fill in for the entire internet, what do Meg and Chris use to fix the server?

question: In the Family Guy episode "How the Griffin Stole Christmas," how much money is each of the remaining employees given in the checks Peter cuts for them?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Herpe, the Love Sore," where are the tough guys shipping out to the following day?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Peterotica," which TV show is parodied by "Quahog Creek"?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Disney's The Reboot," what kind of show does the focus group say they want before Peter pitches one?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to the North Pole", which celebrity appears on a live-action poster on Herbert's wall as the "little drummer boy" Herbert wants for Christmas?
reply: It's Nick Jonas. A live-action poster of him hangs on Herbert's wall in "Road to the North Pole," and during the song "All I Really Want For Christmas" Herbert names him as the "little drummer boy" he wants for Christmas.
source: He appears in live-action on a poster on Herbert's wall in "Road to the North Pole", as the "little drummer boy" he wants for Christmas during the song "All I Really Want For Christmas".

question: In the Family Guy episode "Partial Terms of Endearment," which part of Peter's glasses disappears in a goof right before the 'proud as a peacock' sketch?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Undergrounded", what kind of animal is Sally, whom Peter finds while digging a tunnel?
reply: Sally is a salamander. In "Undergrounded", Lois grounds Peter, so he digs a tunnel from the Griffin home to The Drunken Clam and finds Sally along the way.
source: Sally is a salamander that Peter finds when digging a tunnel from the Griffin home to The Drunken Clam after being grounded by Lois in "Undergrounded".

question: In the Family Guy episode "Play It Again, Brian," who does Brian aggressively make a pass at?

source: That evening, Brian loses his self-restraint and attempts to make a pass at her aggressively; Lois is greatly troubled by this, possibly not least by her own feelings, so she forces him out of the room.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Lois Comes Out of Her Shell", whose concert is held at the Quahog Civic Center?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Valentine's Day in Quahog," which Gremlins character turns out to be the ex-girlfriend Brian says can't get wet?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Life of Brian", whose funeral does Jillian Russell-Wilcox attend?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Mind Over Murder," what does Peter turn his basement into while under house arrest?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Guy, Robot", which Griffin family member is kidnapped by Buffalo Bill?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Meg Stinks!", which character actually calls Lois a pig after Stewie suggests it for her picking her teeth at the table?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Don't Make Me Over", what does Peter put on to entertain George W. Bush at the White House?

source: Peter is invited to the White House to entertain Bush in "Don't Make Me Over", which he does by donning a clown's red nose, and making a series of silly faces and noises, as if entertaining a young child.

question: In the Family Guy special "Something, Something, Something, Dark Side," which old friend of Han runs Cloud City?

question: What song does Barack Obama perform at James Woods Regional High School's assembly in Family Guy?

question: How many trivia questions are in the Family Guy Trivia Game?

question: Which judge did Family Guy writer Richard Appel work for as a law clerk after law school?

source: Following in his mother's footsteps Appel instead became a lawyer. After attending law school he started out as a law clerk for Judge John M. Walker, Jr.

question: Which Ewok celebration music cue from the original Return of the Jedi plays at the end of the Family Guy episode "It's A Trap!"?

question: In the Family Guy episode "All About Alana," what color has Alana dyed her hair when Lois finds her at breakfast wearing Lois's clothes?

source: When Lois reports for breakfast the next morning, she finds Alana dressed in her clothes with her hair dyed red, but Lois draws the line when she offers to go to the grocery store.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Phony Montana," which couple has Lois rescheduled a double date with so many times that she forgets who they are?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Breaking Out is Hard to Do," the view of Asiantown looks identical to which South Korean city?

question: In the Family Guy episode "3 Acts of God," which country singer do the guys go to see at the Country Music Awards because they believe she has a connection to God?

question: Which U.S. state did Davy Crockett, the frontiersman referenced in Family Guy, represent in Congress?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Rhode Island", which TV show's episode does Stewie ask Brian to tape for him in return for coming along on the trip?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Stewie Kills Lois," which actor does Peter mistakenly think played "the British chick from Titanic"?

source: When Peter and Lois Griffin were on their cruise in "Stewie Kills Lois", Lois felt like "the British chick from Titanic". Peter corrects her, believing the role was played by Philip Seymour Hoffman.

question: On which TV interview program did Seth MacFarlane say the Family Guy theme song lyric "effin' cry" makes no sense?

question: On which Cartoon Network block did Family Guy air with extra scenes and dialogue that were cut from the original FOX broadcasts?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Death Has a Shadow," which item does Lois ask Peter for in a scene that has an animation goof where her feet are the same color as her shoes?

question: In the Family Guy episode "80's Guy", who challenges Stewie to a race to the top of the jungle gym?
reply: Doug does. In "80's Guy" he challenges Stewie to race to the top of the jungle gym to get his frisbee back, with a group of kids watching, the little red-haired girl among them.
source: In "80's Guy", Doug challenges Stewie to a race to the top of the jungle gym to retrieve his frisbee in front of a gathering of kids including the little red-haired girl.

question: At which waterpark does Chris Griffin steal Isabella's top after she loses it on a slide?
reply: It happens at Super Splash City. Isabella loses her top on a slide and Chris takes it, but when she calls him out he finds her attractive, and Stewie talks him into asking her on a date.
source: Chris steals her top after she loses it on a slide at Super Splash City waterpark, but when she calls him on it, he finds her attractive and Stewie convinces him to get a date with her.

question: In which segment of "Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story" does Katie Couric appear and yell at Peter Griffin?
reply: She's in "Bango Was His Name Oh," the second segment of Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story. In it she yells at Peter Griffin for being annoying while she's hosting Today.
source: She appeared in the second segment of Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story, "Bango Was His Name Oh", and yelled at Peter Griffin for being annoying while she was doing Today.

question: Chris Griffin isn't the brightest Griffin, but he becomes surprisingly coherent when he talks about movies with which character?

source:
Personality
Though Chris is not the brightest one in the family, he is particularly coherent and makes a good point when talking about movies with Carl.

question: In the Family Guy episode "And the Wiener is...", which organization does an insecure Peter join?
reply: Peter joins the National Gun Association. He suddenly feels insecure and joins it after his attempt to make up for it with a long red car goes wrong, since the car gets crushed short in a collision just as a bus full of models drives by.
source: Suddenly insecure, Peter tries buying a long, red car, which is caught in a collision and shortened to an extreme amount as a bus full of pretty models drive by, and joins the National Gun Association.

question: At what Quahog venue does Stewie confront Mary Elizabeth Becca Ryan about the downsides of stan culture?
reply: Stewie confronts her at the Quahog Walk of Fame, where she's about to get her handprints done. He's there to call out the downsides of stan culture, but by then she's already over the tweet and hardly remembers it.
source: At the Quahog Walk of Fame, where she is about to receive handprints, Stewie decides to confront MEBR over the cons of stan culture, only to find that she has already gotten over the tweet and barely remembers it.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Chris Cross", which character watches Chris hug his sibling and then drives away to cry about their break-up to some friends?
reply: It's Herbert. In "Chris Cross" he watches the hug and drives off to cry to some friends about their break-up.
source: She apologizes and admits she missed him and Chris admits that they need each other to cope in the family. Herbert watches as they hug and drives away to cry about their break up to some friends.

question: In the Family Guy crossover episode "The Simpsons Guy," which deceased Family Guy character does Peter ask Homer to say hello to?
reply: It's Muriel Goldman. Homer asks Peter to say hello to Maude Flanders, and Peter answers by asking Homer to say hello to Muriel Goldman. Both are characters who died on their own shows.
source: Homer tells Peter to say hello to Maude Flanders, and Peter tells Homer to say hello to Muriel Goldman, both references to characters who have died on their shows. Roger from American Dad!

question: In the Family Guy episode "I Am Peter, Hear Me Roar," what prize are Peter, Lois, and their neighbors promised for attending the time-share sales pitch at the Quahog Airport Inn?
reply: They're promised a boat. In "I Am Peter, Hear Me Roar," Peter, Lois and a lot of their neighbors sit through a high-pressure time-share pitch at the Quahog Airport Inn to get it.
source: The Quahog Airport Inn is where Peter and Lois, as well as many of their neighbors, attend a high-pressure time-share sales pitch in order to be given a boat in "I Am Peter, Hear Me Roar".

question: In the Family Guy episode "The New Adventures of Old Tom", which U.S. president does Brian bring up to justify his scam, pointing out that the president is on Mount Rushmore without having taken part in a major event like the others?
reply: It's Theodore Roosevelt. In "The New Adventures of Old Tom," Brian compares his scam to Roosevelt being on Mount Rushmore even though, unlike the others, he wasn't part of a major event.
source: Brian pursues a scam in "The New Adventures of Old Tom", comparing it to Theodore Roosevelt being on Mount Rushmore without having participated in a major event compared to the others.

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Father, the Son, and the Holy Fonz," which celebrity does a man tell his wife to imagine naked when Stewie rolls by in a bubble?

source: Spencer's Cleaners is located next door to Super Cowboy USA Hot Dog Rocket Ship American Cleaners Number One in Quahog, Rhode Island in "Tiegs for Two".

question: In what year was character actor Michael Pataki born?
reply: He was born in 1938, on January 16 to be exact. Pataki was an American character actor who appeared in Rocky IV, Halloween 4 and Star Trek, and he died on April 15, 2010.
source: Michael Pataki (January 16, 1938 – April 15, 2010) was an American character actor, known for his roles in Rocky IV, Halloween 4: The Return of Michael Myers, Star Trek, Combat!, Rawhide, Batman, Mission: Impossible, Happy Days, Little House on the Prairie and Star Trek: The Next Generation.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Brian: Portrait of a Dog," which character is seen singing "Anything Goes"?
reply: Lois Griffin sings "Anything Goes." It happens when Brian gets out of the car after Peter humiliates him at the Quahog Dog Show.
source: On Family Guy, Lois Griffin is seen singing "Anything Goes" when Brian gets out of the car after Peter humiliates him at the Quahog Dog Show in "Brian: Portrait of a Dog".

question: About how many performances does Carnegie Hall present each season?
reply: Carnegie Hall puts on about 250 performances each season. It has its own artistic programming, development and marketing departments, and it also rents the hall out to performing groups.
source: Carnegie Hall has its own artistic programming, development, and marketing departments, and presents about 250 performances each season. It is also rented out to performing groups.

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Talented Mr. Stewie," which Michelle Obama book does Stewie read?
reply: Stewie reads Michelle Obama's memoir *Becoming* in "The Talented Mr. Stewie."
source: Donna prank calls Cleveland in "A House Full of Peters" by pretending to be Michelle. Stewie reads Becoming by Michelle Obama in "The Talented Mr. Stewie".

question: In the Family Guy episode "Take This Job and Love It," what is the name of the international spy Peter imagines being as his dream job?
reply: The spy is called Lap Band. When Joe gets everyone to share what their dream job would have been, Peter pictures himself as Lap Band, an international spy on the run from Finnish agents.
page: Take This Job and Love It
source: This gives Joe the idea for everyone to share what their dream job would have been. Peter imagines himself as an international spy named Lap Band, who is on the run from Finnish agents.

question: Which Family Guy episode was moved up to air on January 16, 2011, replacing "The Hand That Rocks the Wheelchair" in its original slot?
reply: It was "And I'm Joyce Kinney," which got moved up and took the January 16, 2011 slot. That pushed "The Hand That Rocks the Wheelchair" back to January 23. It was bumped again that week and finally aired on March 6.
page: The Hand That Rocks the Wheelchair
source: The episode was originally meant to air on January 16, 2011, but was replaced with the moved-up "And I'm Joyce Kinney", pushing it back to January 23, 2011, but was replaced by a repeat of "Brian Writes a Bestseller", pushing it back again to March 6.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Whistle While Your Wife Works", which character tries to convince Brian to break up with Jillian Russell?
reply: Stewie does it. He's outraged that Brian wants to date such an airhead and tries to get him to break up with her, but Brian ends up sleeping with Jillian instead.

Although he appears to feel sorry for her, he reluctantly admits that her induced purging makes her body look "fantastic."

In "Whistle While Your Wife Works", Stewie, outraged that Brian wants to date such an airhead, tries to convince him to break up with her, but Brian ends up having sex with her instead.

question: In which Family Guy episode did Tom Bosley voice himself in a Happy Days segment?
answers: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Fonz
The Father, the Son and the Holy Fonz
reply: Tom Bosley voiced himself in "The Father, the Son, and the Holy Fonz," in a bit from Happy Days. He's also mentioned in "Road to Europe," where Stewie thinks he's on the same train as Bosley.
source: Stewie Griffin thought he was riding the same train as Bosley in "Road to Europe". He voiced himself in "The Father, the Son, and the Holy Fonz" in an episode of Happy Days.

question: In Family Guy, which film inspired the movie "Steel Vaginas"?
reply: "Steel Vaginas" was inspired by Autumn's Piano, a film of the same genre. The director watched it with his wife, and she was later cast as the female lead.
source: The film was inspired by Autumn's Piano, a film considered to be of the same genre that the director saw with his wife, who would later be cast as the female lead.

question: In what year did the U.S. Supreme Court decide Community for Creative Non-Violence v. Reid, the copyright case about the meaning of "employee"?
reply: The Supreme Court decided Community for Creative Non-Violence v. Reid, 490 U.S. 730, in 1989. It held that in copyright law, "employee" should be read using common law agency principles.
source: In Community for Creative Non-Violence v. Reid, 490 U.S. 730 (1989), the Supreme Court held that the term "employee" in this context should be interpreted according to common law agency principles.

question: In the Family Guy episode "A Hero Sits Next Door," what TV show does Lois put on for Stewie after she takes away his copy of The Art of War?
reply: She puts on the Teletubbies. Stewie had picked up The Art of War after deciding The Prince taught him nothing new, but Lois caught him, took the book away and turned on the show for him.
source: In "A Hero Sits Next Door", after being disappointed that The Prince taught him nothing new, Stewie picked up The Art of War to read, but Lois caught him and took it away, turning on the Teletubbies instead.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Old West," what does Cleveland ride with the posse because he couldn't get a horse?
reply: He rides his bike. The others had already taken the last three horses, so Cleveland couldn't buy one for the posse.
source: Cleveland was unable to buy a horse for the posse as the others had already nabbed the remaining three, so he instead settled for riding his bike. Joe's favorite TV cop is Harry Bosch.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Death Is a Bitch", which Titanic character played by Kate Winslet appears?
reply: She shows up as Rose from Titanic in "Death Is a Bitch." The episode uses Jack as an example of someone saved because death no longer exists, and he tells Rose he has a girlfriend in New York.
source: She appeared as Rose from Titanic in "Death Is a Bitch", when Jack, having been used as an example of a person saved by the nonexistence of death, tells her he has a girlfriend in New York.

question: Which member of the music group Black Box was a classically trained clarinet teacher?
reply: Valerio Semplici was Black Box's classically trained clarinet teacher. The other two in the trio were club DJ Daniele Davoli and Mirko Limoni, who was the keyboard and electronic music "wiz."
source: The members of the group included a trio made up of a club DJ (Daniele Davoli), a classically trained clarinet teacher (Valerio Semplici), and a keyboard and electronic music "wiz" (Mirko Limoni).

question: Sebastian Maniscalco is a stand-up comedian who has appeared in Family Guy. On what date was he born?
reply: Sebastian Maniscalco was born on July 8, 1973. He's an American stand-up comedian and actor, and he also had supporting roles in Green Book and The Irishman.
source: Sebastian Maniscalco (born July 8, 1973) is an American stand-up comedian and actor who also had supporting acting roles in the films Green Book and The Irishman.

question: In the Disney film Pinocchio, who appointed Jiminy Cricket to be Pinocchio's official conscience?
reply: It was the Blue Fairy. In Disney's Pinocchio she made Jiminy Cricket Pinocchio's official conscience, and he's appeared many more times since that first film.
source: He was appointed by the Blue Fairy in the Disney film to serve as Pinocchio's official conscience. Since his debut in Pinocchio, he made numerous other appearances.

question: Which Family Guy episode did the Parents Television Council name "Worst TV Show of the Week," partly over a gag showing God with a prostitute?
reply: It was "The Courtship of Stewie's Father." Part of the reason the Parents Television Council named it "Worst TV Show of the Week" was a gag that showed God as a dirty old man having sex with a prostitute while he brushed off a teenage Jesus, who wanted help with a fight he was having with Joseph.
source: For instance, "The Courtship of Stewie's Father" was named "Worst TV Show of the Week" in part due to a gag that depicted God as a dirty old man having sex with a prostitute all while brushing off a teen-aged Jesus, who was seeking some help with his quarrel with Joseph.

question: In Family Guy, which rival company's pie recipe does Carter Pewterschmidt order Lois to steal after Big Pie comes second in the annual pie rankings?
reply: Lois was sent after the recipe for Aunt Maude's Pies. Carter was furious that his company only came second in the annual pie rankings, so he ordered her to go to Townsville and steal it so he could drive Aunt Maude's out of business and take the #1 spot.
source: After Carter is outraged about the company coming in second on annual pie rankings, he orders Lois to travel to Townsville and steal the recipe for Aunt Maude's Pies in order to drive them out of business and claim the #1 spot.

question: In the DVD commentary for the Family Guy episode "Jungle Love", the writers said they like which actor but felt let down by him over a film remake?
reply: It was Ferrell. In the "Jungle Love" DVD commentary, the writers said they like him, but they hated the film remake and felt he let them down.
source: The writers of the show stated in the DVD commentary for this episode that they like Ferrell, but they hated the film remake and felt let down by him.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Bango Was His Name Oh", Quagmire's hair is styled like his Navy-era look shown in which earlier episode?
reply: It's "Death Lives." In "Bango Was His Name Oh," when Stewie first finds Quagmire chained to the bed, Quagmire's hair is cut the same way it was in his Navy days as shown in "Death Lives."
source: When Stewie first finds Quagmire chained to the bed, Quagmire’s hair is cut the same way it was when he was in the Navy as shown on the episode “Death Lives”.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Grumpy Old Man", Peter says it would have been better if which real-life person had retired, mistaking his drive to prove his innocence for work?
reply: It's John Bennett Ramsey. In "Grumpy Old Man", Peter says it would have been better if Ramsey had retired, because he mixes up Ramsey's determination to prove his innocence with a job.
source: In "Grumpy Old Man", Peter states it would have been better if John Bennett Ramsey would've retired, confusing his determination to prove his innocence for work.

question: In Family Guy, Lois asks if she and Peter can tag along on a picnic so Peter can be reminded what romance is like. Whose picnic is it?
reply: It's Heather and Chris's picnic. Lois asks to come along so Peter can be reminded what romance is like, but his stupidity keeps backfiring on her.
source: After finding out that Heather and Chris have a picnic planned, Lois asks if she and Peter can tag along so Peter can be reminded what romance is like, but his stupidity repeatedly backfires in Lois' face.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Running Mates," who wins the election in a landslide?
reply: Peter wins it. His ad works and he's elected in a landslide, and then a furious Lois tells him he'd better do something worthwhile as president besides reinstating a crazy teacher.

question: In the Family Guy "HBO-No" parody of Big Little Lies, which celebrity are all the women dressed as while Wild West searches for the culprit?

Big Little Lies
When a smelly pile of poop is discovered at the bottom of a school staircase, Wild West sets out to discover the culprit, but has issues because all of the men are dressed as Audrey Hepburn, and all of the women are dressed as Elvis.

question: In which comic book did the Marvel superhero Spider-Man, who is referenced on Family Guy, make his first appearance?

question: In the Family Guy episode "A Shot in the Dark," what does Cleveland go on television to force Quahog to consider the incident?
reply: Cleveland wants it treated as a hate crime. In "A Shot in the Dark," he cuts ties with Peter and goes on TV to push Quahog to call it one, even though Joe explains that the police think it was an accident.
source: As Joe tries to explain that the police have considered it an accident, Cleveland refuses to have anything further to do with Peter, going on television to force the city of Quahog to consider it a hate crime.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Ratings Guy", which character mocks Fire Captain Beckman's firefighters for having hoses instead of guns during an open house?

source: During an open house in "Ratings Guy", he has to contend with Joe Swanson who ridicules the fire fighters for having hoses instead of guns and shoots the tires of their firetruck as he says he'll see them on the softball field.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Deep Throats", which character asks for a ride from Brian, who is working as a cab driver, and gets passed over?
reply: It's Cleveland Brown. In "Deep Throats", Brian is a cab driver, and he passes on Cleveland when Cleveland asks for a ride.

question: Which college did Family Guy director Zac Moncrief attend after leaving his hometown in 1989?
reply: Zac Moncrief went to the California Institute of the Arts, which Disney funded and which focuses on animation. He left his small hometown of Montvale, New Jersey, to start there in 1989.
source: Zac Moncrief left his small hometown of Montvale, New Jersey, in 1989 to go to California Institute of the Arts, a Disney-funded college specializing in animation.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Germany", what campaign item does Stewie Griffin find in his Adolf Hitler disguise?
reply: He finds a McCain/Palin campaign button. Stewie comes across it in his Adolf Hitler disguise in "Road to Germany."
source: In "Road to Germany", Stewie Griffin finds a McCain/Palin campaign button in his Adolf Hitler disguise. In "Brian & Stewie", it is revealed that Brian voted for McCain.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Valentine's Day in Quahog", which character gathers Brian's former girlfriends, including Miss Emily, to find out why Brian is unsuccessful in love?
reply: Stewie did it. In "Valentine's Day in Quahog" he rounds up a lot of Brian's ex-girlfriends, Miss Emily among them, to work out why Brian keeps failing at love.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Holy Crap," Peter tells Francis his favorite book of the Bible is the one where Jesus swallows a puzzle piece. Which children's book is that joke referencing?
answers: Curious George Goes to the Hospital
reply: It's a nod to Curious George Goes to the Hospital by Margret and H.A. Peter mixes up the Bible with that kids' book and describes Jesus swallowing a puzzle piece before the man in the big yellow hat takes him to the hospital.

This a reference to the children's book, Curious George Goes to the Hospital by Margret and H.A.

question: In the Family Guy parody of Family Feud in Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story, groping a female contestant spoofs which Family Feud host, who always kissed the female contestants?

source: Goode", the first segment of Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story, cops a feel from one of the female contestants ala Richard Dawson, who always kissed the ladies on the show.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Fertilized Megg," William tells Stewie to call him by the name of which 1979 Sally Field film character?

source: In "Fertilized Megg", William tells Stewie to "...call me Norma Rae because you're about to see a strike", referring to the 1979 film starring Sally Field in the titular role, who leads a strike in a textile factory over poor working conditions.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Partial Terms of Endearment," Peter references the premise of which sequel film, in which the heroes must save a rec center from being torn down for a mall?

source: The 80s Black Guys Ozone and Turbo are the male leads of the film Breakin while Peter references the premise of the sequel Breakin' 2: Electric Boogaloo where they must save the rec center from getting torn down to be replaced by a mall

question: In the Family Guy episode "Fecal Matters," which ballpark does Peter Griffin go to so he can pretend to be a Boston Red Sox player?
reply: He goes to Fenway Park. A bad flu leaves Peter as one of the only people still up and about in the Eastern United States, so he heads there to play at being a Boston Red Sox player.
source: When Peter finds himself one of the only active persons in the Eastern United States after a severe bout of the flu in "Fecal Matters", he goes to Fenway Park to pretend that he's a Boston Red Sox baseball player.

question: In the Family Guy "Rock Lobster" gag, Peter seems to be the only one playing guitar. What kind of guitars are actually heard in the chorus?

source: Even though Peter is shown to be the only one playing the guitar, it's actually two six-string acoustic guitars in the verses, and two 12-string guitars in the chorus.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Pitch Imperfect," during which Quahog 5 News segment did porn accidentally air, prompting Tom Tucker to apologize?
reply: It aired during the cooking segment. Tom Tucker apologized for the Quahog 5 News team and blamed it on some team members who are too good with computers.
source: Tom Tucker apologizes on behalf of the Quahog 5 News team due to some porn that aired during the network's cooking segment, which he blames on some team members who are too good with computers.

question: Between 2002 and 2006, roughly how many Family Guy episodes did Sarah Frost work on as a director, assistant director, or art director?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Bookie of the Year," how much does Peter bet a heckler that Chris will get the strikeout in his first game pitching?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Brian in Love," what do Lois and Peter decide Stewie is ready for after the living room carpet is found wet?
reply: They decide he's ready for potty training. Stewie insists he didn't wet the living room carpet, but Lois and Peter take the wet spot as a sign that it's time.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Family Cat," who does Meg share an intimate dance with as their relationship grows?
reply: Meg dances with Pouncy. As they grow closer they share an intimate dance, and later that night Pouncy leads Meg out of the house.
source: Meg's relationship with Pouncy advances until they share an intimate dance, and later that night, Pouncy leads her out of the house under her control.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Seahorse Seashell Party," what body part does Brian cut off while tripping?

source: When Brian starts to trip out he leaves and is followed by Stewie who observes him cutting off his own ear. Patching him up, Stewie sticks by Brian while he trips, seeing weird and disturbing things.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Peter's Lost Youth," what injury does Lois suffer when Peter slides into her at second base?
reply: A broken leg. Lois was playing second base and Peter was running against her, and when he tried to impress the guys with his slide, he ended up breaking her leg.
source: When Lois is selected to play second base while Peter is chosen to run against her, his attempt to impress the guys with his slide ends up breaking Lois' leg.

question: Since what year has Fenway Park been the home ballpark of the Boston Red Sox?
reply: 1912. The Boston Red Sox were founded in 1901 as one of the American League's eight charter franchises, and they've played their home games at Fenway Park since 1912.
source: Founded in 1901 as one of the American League's eight charter franchises, the Red Sox's home ballpark has been Fenway Park since 1912. The "Red Sox" name was chosen by the team owner, John I.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Baby, It's Cold Inside," what film's calavera appears on the candle accompanying the flowers Peter steals from a roadside memorial for Lois?

source: Peter's first two attempts to make his shortcomings up to Lois include getting her in the opening credits for Saturday Night Live and stealing flowers from a roadside memorial, accompanied by a candle with a calavera from the film Coco.

question: For his role as which mobster in Goodfellas did Joe Pesci win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor?
reply: Joe Pesci won for playing mobster Tommy DeVito in Goodfellas. He took home the Best Supporting Actor Oscar in 1990, ten years after he was nominated in the same category for Raging Bull.

question: In the musical Miss Saigon, which is referenced in Family Guy, during what war is the plot set?

source: The setting of the plot is relocated to 1970s Saigon during the Vietnam War, and Madame Butterfly's American Lieutenant and Japanese geisha coupling is replaced by a romance between an American GI and a Vietnamese bar girl.

question: Who directed the 1989 action film Road House, starring Patrick Swayze?

source: Road House is a 1989 American action film directed by Rowdy Herrington and starring Patrick Swayze and Sam Elliott as bouncers at a seedy roadside bar who protect a small town in Missouri from a corrupt businessman.

question: The repeated "fa la la" in the carol "Deck the Halls" is also used in which older song?
reply: It's "Nos Galan." The "fa la la" refrain comes from medieval ballads, but the rest of the "Deck the Halls" lyrics are American and date from the nineteenth century.
source: The repeated "fa la la" is from medieval ballads and used in "Nos Galan", the remaining lyrics are American in origin dating from the nineteenth century.

question: In the Family Guy episode "One if by Clam, Two if by Sea," which 19th-century British Prime Minister appears in a cutaway saying "You don't even know who I am"?
reply: It's Benjamin Disraeli, the 19th-century British Prime Minister, statesman and writer. In a quick cutaway he says "You don't even know who I am," which is the show making fun of its own habit of referencing people many viewers have never heard of.
page: One if by Clam, Two if by Sea
source: Benjamin Disraeli, the 19th Century British Prime Minister, statesman and literary figure, is seen in a brief cutaway in which he states, “You don’t even know who I am.” With this, Family Guy pokes fun at itself referencing not only well-known pop culture icons and historical figures, but also relatively obscure people of whom many viewers have no knowledge.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Rhode Island," how many gun holes are visible above Stewie and Brian's motel bed in the morning, even though only five were there the night before?
reply: I count seven gun holes. When Stewie wakes up to answer the phone in "Road to Rhode Island," seven holes show above the bed, though only five were there during the night. It's a continuity goof.
source: During the night at the motel, five gun holes are clearly visible above Stewie and Brian's bed. In the morning when Stewie wakes up to answer the phone, there are seven gun shot holes above the bed.

question: In "Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story," what is the name of the ranting segment Peter hosts at Quahog 5 News?

question: In Family Guy, who told Brian and Stewie about Dylan Flannigan when they went to visit her?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Joe's Revenge," who does Peter convince Joe to go after with the guys?

question: According to the DVD commentary for the Family Guy episode "In Harmony's Way," which Utah-based choir, along with the Harlem Boys Choir, is the "All Five-Foot-One Black Albino Choir" meant to reference?

question: In Family Guy, what does Stewie shout for Brian to do as Bingo the Dingo carries him off?

question: In the Drawn Together episode "The Lemon-AIDS Walk", what does Wooldoor get briefly detained for stealing?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Passenger Fatty-Seven," Peter asks the animators to turn the guys into characters from which franchise?

question: In which Family Guy episode do the Griffin kids look back fondly on Peter's antics and bring up the Hindenpeter?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Take a Letter," which song's hook does Stewie make when he thinks he might be able to get Chadley's wallet?

question: In the Family Guy episode "A Picture's Worth a Thousand Bucks," which Murphy Brown character does Faith Ford voice in a cutaway?

source: In another cutaway, former Murphy Brown stars Candice Bergen (as Murphy), Faith Ford (as Corky Sherwood), Joe Regalbuto (as Frank Fontana), and Charles Kimbrough (as Jim Dial) inject dated “buzzwords” into a nondescript conversation, poking fun at the show’s topical humor.

question: Karen Black appeared in which Alfred Hitchcock film, his last one?
reply: Karen Black was in Family Plot, the last film Alfred Hitchcock made. She's also known for Easy Rider, Five Easy Pieces, The Great Gatsby, Nashville and Airport 1975.
source: She was noted for appearing in such films as Easy Rider, Five Easy Pieces, The Great Gatsby, The Day of the Locust, Nashville, Airport 1975, and Alfred Hitchcock's final film, Family Plot.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Run, Chris, Run," which character gives Cleveland a beer and bonds with him over drinks after the guys stick Cleveland with the bill at the Clam?

question: In the Family Guy episode "A Hero Sits Next Door," Peter says "Me love you long time" to a Japanese baseball player. Which film is that line from?

question: In the Family Guy episode "German Guy," what rank's stripes appear on Herbert's old World War II uniform, contradicting his claim to have been a Lieutenant?

source: Herbert claims to have been a Lieutenant in World War II. However, when he puts his old uniform on later in the episode, it has corporal's stripes on the sleeves.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Rupert," which school does Stanford say he attended after Stewie tells him Brian will lick peanut butter off any part of his body?

source: When Stewie tells Stanford that Brian will lick peanut butter off any part of his body, Stanford pauses momentarily before saying, “Well I did go to Choate,” referring to Choate Rosemary Hall, a New England prepatory school.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Baby Not On Board," what does Carl offer Peter Griffin to avoid a lawsuit?

source: He was threatened by Chris' father Peter in "Baby Not On Board" when Chris makes a sexual remark to Peter and exposes himself to him. To avoid a lawsuit, Carl offers him an unlimited gas card.

question: The Family Guy episode "Meet the Quagmires" draws on which chaos theory concept, also called "sensitive dependence on initial conditions"?

question: In Family Guy, which country was Brittney Griner returned from in a trade that angers Peter Griffin?

question: In The A-Team, a TV series referenced on Family Guy, the group of soldiers of fortune were formerly members of which branch of the US Army?
reply: They were US Army Special Forces. In the show, the ex-soldiers work as soldiers of fortune while running from the military, which branded them war criminals for a "crime they didn't commit."
source: The A-Team is an American action adventure television series about a fictional group of ex-United States Army Special Forces who work as soldiers of fortune while being on the run from the military after being branded as war criminals for a "crime they didn't commit".

question: In the Family Guy episode "Coma Guy," Peter hallucinates a cruise ship full of dead characters, Charles Yamamoto among them. Which canal is that ship sailing through?
reply: It's the Panama Canal. In "Coma Guy," Charles Yamamoto, who is voiced by Robert Wu, shows up in Peter's hallucination of a cruise ship full of dead characters going through the Panama Canal.
source: Charles is voiced by Robert Wu. He is seen in a hallucination of Peter's on a cruise ship full of deceased characters in the Panama Canal in "Coma Guy".

question: In the Family Guy episode "Brian Sings and Swings," which celebrity is Brian talking to while drunk before a goof shows Brian suddenly sober on stage?

source: After Frank Sinatra Jr. is finished speaking to a drunk Brian, he goes on stage and when the camera cuts to Brian finishing his drink, joining Frank on stage, he appears as his normal, sober self.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Customer of the Week", which family member accuses the staff of going easy on Seth MacFarlane's voice while characters like the Kool-Aid Man stand by mute?

source: When Meg accuses the staff of taking it easy on Seth MacFarlane's voice in "Customer of the Week", several characters that he voices, including the Kool-Aid Man, stand by mute.

question: Which grade did Mrs. Wilson teach Peter Griffin in when he was a child in Family Guy?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Emmy-Winning Episode," which actress voices Shonda Rhimes?

question: What is the birth date of Shaquille O'Neal, the basketball star who has appeared in Family Guy?

source: Shaquille Rashaun O'Neal (born March 6, 1972), nicknamed "Shaq", is an American retired professional basketball player who is a sports analyst and actor.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Girlfriend, Eh?", which Griffin family member does Lois end up competing with for the same man's attention?

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Courtship of Stewie's Father," which Indiana Jones character does Stewie dress as during the mineshaft chase parody?

question: On what date was voice actor Stephen Stanton born?
reply: Stephen Stanton was born on August 22, 1961. He's a German-born American voice actor, impressionist, visual effects artist and comedian who does voice work for video games, movies and TV shows.
source: Stephen W. Stanton (born August 22, 1961) is a German-born American voice actor, impressionist, visual effects artist and comedian, known for his voice over work in video games, movies and TV shows.

question: In Family Guy, which two characters spy on a couple's date at Di & Rhea's Indian Cuisine?

question: Under United States copyright law, against whom is an award of attorney's fees not available?

question: Under United States copyright law, what term describes the losses a copyright holder actually suffers because of an infringement?
reply: The term is "actual damages." Under United States copyright law, these are the losses the copyright holder really suffers because of the infringement. They are separate from "profits," which are what the infringer gains from it.
source: Actual damages are the actual losses suffered by the copyright holder as a result of the infringement. Profits are the profits gained by the wrongdoer as a result of the infringement.

reply: He's a traffic cop. In 2035 Chris has also married Vanessa, a hateful, foul-mouthed hustler who belittles him and wants Peter and Lois put in a retirement home.
source: In the year 2035 at a family dinner, Stewie discovers how the lives of his family will pan out: Chris will become a traffic cop and marry a hateful, foul-mouthed hustler named Vanessa who belittles him and insists on putting Peter and Lois in a retirement home; Meg will transition from female to male after college and lives as a man named Ron; and Brian will die by eating chocolate he found in the garbage, go to Heaven, and spend a rather promising eternity drinking with Ernest Hemingway, Vincent van Gogh and Kurt Cobain.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Tales of a Third Grade Nothing," what is Peter sent upstairs to deliver to the CEO?

source: Peter is sent upstairs by his boss to deliver shipping reports to the CEO. On his way to deliver the reports, he decides to go into the executive bathroom.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Brokeback Swanson," the mental patient Gary lives at which institution?

source: Gary is a mental patient at the Quahog State Home. In "Brokeback Swanson", when the guys decide to help Joe leave, he notes that he will be happy to get away from people screaming in his face.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Bango Was His Name Oh", what object does Peter identify as the Holy Grail in an Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade reference?

question: In the Caillou episode Lois watches on Family Guy, what does Caillou think he is because he's bald?
reply: Caillou thinks he's a cancer patient because he's bald. Lois falls asleep watching it, then calls the episodes dull, though she doesn't find any cursing in them.
source: As part of an episode is shown where Caillou thinks he's a cancer patient because he's bald, Lois ends up falling asleep and later calls the episodes dull, but finds no evidence of cursing.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Patriot Games", Peter thinks his new team is a bunch of "softies". Which team does he set up a game between them and the Patriots?

source: Peter is disgusted to discover they are a bunch of 'softies' but decides to turn them around and stages a game between the Silly Nannies and the Patriots.

question: In the Family Guy episode "All About Alana", which TV show's catchphrase does Lois parody when she says "You wouldn't like me when I'm groceries"?

In "All About Alana", Lois says, "You wouldn't like me when I'm groceries", parodying the catchphrase from the television show The Incredible Hulk. External Links

question: Which actor reprised his role as Dr. Gregory House for a cameo in the Family Guy episode "Business Guy"?

source: Dr. Gregory House from the FOX show House, M.D. makes a cameo appearance in the episode. Hugh Laurie, who portrays him on the show, reprised his role.

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Splendid Source," who did Cleveland hear the dirty joke from while on a trip to Washington D.C.?
reply: He heard it from Sal. Peter, Joe and Quagmire traced the joke back to Cleveland in Stoolbend, Virginia, and found out he'd picked it up from Sal on a trip to Washington D.C. with Cleveland, Jr.
source: In "The Splendid Source", Peter, Joe and Quagmire trace a dirty joke back to Cleveland in Stoolbend, Virginia and find he heard it from Sal while on a trip with Cleveland, Jr. to Washington D.C..

question: In the Family Guy episode "Brian Goes Back to College," what was Brian's teacher planning to do before Brian inspired him?
reply: He was planning to commit suicide. Brian went to admit that he'd cheated, but the teacher cut him off and said Brian had inspired him after he'd been so depressed.
source: Brian goes to tell his teacher that he cheated, but was interrupted, and the teacher tells him Brian has inspired him, and he was so depressed that he was planning to commit suicide.

question: In the Family Guy episode "No Chris Left Behind," which upper-class school does Carter Pewterschmidt use his influence to get Chris into?
reply: Morningwood Academy. Lois tried several other schools for Chris first and they all fell through, so she asked her father, Carter, to use his influence to get Chris into the upper-class academy.
source: After several failed attempts to find another school for Chris, Lois asks her father, Carter, to use his influence to get Chris admitted to the upper-class Morningwood Academy.

question: In what year was comedian Foster Brooks, who is referenced in Family Guy, born?
reply: Foster Brooks was born on May 11, 1912. He was an American actor and comedian, best known for his nightclub acts and TV appearances, and he died on December 20, 2001.
source: Foster Brooks (May 11, 1912 – December 20, 2001) was an American actor and comedian, notable for his nightclub performances and appearances in television programs.

question: At the end of the Family Guy episode "Brian Wallows and Peter's Swallows", in which bar do Brian and Peter sit talking over their losses?
reply: They're at The Drunken Clam. A good-looking woman and a bird that acts like a person come up to them there, but Brian and Peter both say they aren't ready yet.
source: In the end, both Brian and Peter are at The Drunken Clam elaborating their losses and are approached by a good looking woman and an anthropomorphic bird, and declare not to be ready yet.

question: In the Family Guy episode "How the Griffin Stole Christmas," which character builds a stuffed bear named Cindy at Build-a-Bear?
reply: Joe Swanson made Cindy, a stuffed bear, at Build-a-Bear in "How the Griffin Stole Christmas." That's also the episode where Peter won't stop playing Santa even after Santa tells him to quit, and the two end up in a prank war.
source: Cindy is a stuffed bear that Joe builds at Build-a-Bear in "How the Griffin Stole Christmas". When Peter refuses to heed Santa's orders to quit portraying him, they engage in a war of pranks.

question: In the Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story segment "Stu & Stewie's Excellent Adventure," which historical figure does Stu Griffin say he went back to see on a previous time travel vacation?

source: Stu Griffin in Stewie Griffin: The Untold Story segment "Stu & Stewie's Excellent Adventure", explains time travel vacations to his younger self by relating his previous vacation to biblical times, when he went back to see Jesus Christ.

source: After Chris shows signs of boils, one of the ten Plagues of Egypt, one of the names Peter said kids used to call him was "Rootin' Tootin' Raspberry." This is a reference to the Pillsbury Funny Face Drink flavor.

question: After Peter and Lois don't appear in the Family Guy episode "Brian & Stewie," which character is left as the only one to have appeared in every episode?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Rupert," what event leads to Brian accidentally selling Stewie's teddy bear Rupert?
reply: It happens at a yard sale. While the Griffins are holding one, Brian accidentally sells Rupert, Stewie's beloved teddy bear, and after he admits it the two of them go looking for the bear.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Stewie Kills Lois," which character scoffs at Stewie, doubting he'll follow through on his diabolical plans?
reply: Brian scoffs at Stewie. He points out that Stewie has never followed through on any of his diabolical plans before, so he doesn't believe Stewie will this time either.
source: Brian scoffs, noting that Stewie has never followed through with any of his diabolical plans before, and is completely skeptical that he will do so this time.

question: When Odo appears in Family Guy, which of his trademark features is oddly missing from his look?
reply: His exaggerated, simplified facial features are missing. Odo is known for very hollow eye sockets and ears that are just two simple holes, but oddly he doesn't have them in his Family Guy scene.
source: Curiously, Odo does not appear with exaggerated or simplified facial features such as extremely hollow eye sockets and ears with only two simple holes in the scene, which is what the character was known for.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Untitled Griffin Family History," a billboard reveals that Danny Gans was named what around the time Moses Griffin freed the Jews from Egypt?

source: In "Untitled Griffin Family History", it was revealed via billboard that he was named Entertainer of the Year around the time that Moses Griffin liberated the Jews from slavery in Egypt.

question: In the Family Guy story "The Candidate", which state does Mayor Wild West travel to when he finds the missing group?
reply: He finds them in Florida. Mayor Wild West saves them from an alligator there and brings everyone home safely.
source: When reports of their disappearance reach Mayor Wild West, he sets out to find them. He finds them down in Florida and rescues them from an alligator, bringing them all home safely.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Halloween on Spooner Street," what game does Bill Clinton play at James Woods Regional High School's unofficial Halloween party?
reply: He plays spin-the-bottle. In "Halloween on Spooner Street," Bill Clinton goes to James Woods Regional High School's unofficial Halloween party dressed up as someone who looks like him.
source: In "Halloween on Spooner Street", Clinton attends James Woods Regional High School's unofficial Halloween party and plays spin-the-bottle. He disguised himself as someone who looks like him.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Love Thy Trophy", which baby is passed off to restaurateur Flappy as a crack-addicted baby so the "single mother" can earn bigger tips?
reply: It's Stewie. She lets Flappy believe Stewie is her crack-addicted baby and that she's a single mother, so people will tip her more. One customer even feels so sorry for Stewie that they ask for her address.
source: She lets restaurateur Flappy believe that Stewie is her crack-addicted baby and she is a single mother, so that people will give her bigger tips, which leads to one of the customers asking for her address feeling sorry for Stewie.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Jesus, Mary & Joseph", which Electric Light Orchestra song plays during the Ben Him & Ben Her scene?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Tales of a Third Grade Nothing," why does John Wilkes Booth prepare to shoot Abraham Lincoln?
reply: Because Lincoln's hat is too tall. In "Tales of a Third Grade Nothing," Booth can't see past it, so he pulls out a gun and gets ready to shoot Abraham in the head.
source: He later appeared in "Tales of a Third Grade Nothing", where he is shown taking out a gun and preparing to shoot Abraham in the head because his hat is too tall and he can't see.

question: What low-budget independent film marked Elizabeth Banks' film debut?

source: Elizabeth Banks (born Elizabeth Irene Mitchell; February 10, 1974) is an American actress. Banks made her film debut in the low-budget independent film Surrender Dorothy.

question: The Family Guy episode title "Stewie B. Goode" is a reference to which Chuck Berry song?

A cutaway shows Stewie as “Short Round” from Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.

question: In which Family Guy episode does Consuela the maid make her first appearance?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Spies Reminiscent of Us," which U.S. president commissioned Chevy Chase and Dan Aykroyd as government spies?

question: In the Family Guy episode "First Blood," what TV show's rerun does Peter need to watch before he can fall asleep?
reply: It's Frasier. In "First Blood," Peter can't fall asleep until he's watched a Frasier rerun.
source: Joe's attempt at counting sheep results in his disabled sheep suing the farmer for ADA violations and taking over the farm. Peter can't go to sleep without rearing a rerun of Frasier.

question: According to Carter Pewterschmidt, what is the secret to happiness?
reply: For Carter Pewterschmidt, money is the secret to happiness, not love. He only rethinks that briefly when he goes broke and Peter helps him rebuild his fortune.
source: To him, money, not love, is the secret to happiness, although he briefly reconsiders his stance when he is penniless and Peter is helping him rebuild his fortune.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Germany", what condition does Nancy Astor find Winston Churchill in?
reply: He's drunk. In "Road to Germany", Nancy Astor comes across Winston Churchill while he's drunk. It's a nod to the famous "I shall be sober in the morning" line, though in real life Churchill said that to Labour MP Bessie Braddock, not to Astor.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Baby, You Knock Me Out," Deirdre Jackson's appearance at Lois' retirement parodies which Rocky III character?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Death Has a Shadow," which family member does Peter decide to keep his firing a secret from?

source: The company receives bad press after releasing unsafe toy products, and Peter is promptly fired. At dinner, he breaks the news to his children, but decides to keep it from Lois.

question: In "Take This Job and Love It," where is the drug bust that Maniac urges Cleveland to go to with him?

question: In Family Guy, after Meg returns home without getting her Green Mountain College interview, whose company wears her out until she decides to get an interview by herself?

question: The title of the Family Guy episode "Mind Over Murder" is a reference to what phrase?

The title is a reference to the phrase "mind over matter."

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Big Bang Theory," what animal does Yousef play a flute for at the farmer's market?

source: When he goes to the farmer's market to buy more plutonium for his time machine return pad in "The Big Bang Theory", Yousef cracks jokes about his terrorist son and wife, punctuated by playing a flute for his dancing cobra in a basket.

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Chicken or the Meg," which song does "When a Girl Loves a Chicken" parody?

Meg and Nugget recreate the spaghetti scene from Lady and The Tramp with a worm.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Death Has a Shadow," which drunk party guest was the leading scorer in Glenn Quagmire's drinking game at his stag party?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Holy Crap", Peter Griffin takes his father Francis to a game at McCoy Stadium. Which team's home game do they see?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Road to Rupert," which televangelist is left behind after the rapture along with Pat Robertson?

question: In the Family Guy episode "It Takes a Village Idiot, and I Married One," which film is parodied in a scene where Brian inexplicably has all his fur back?

source: In the Amadeus parody scene, Brian has all of his fur back despite having lost the majority of it in the lake with the rest of the family. He is shown with a powdered wig like everyone else, however.

question: Which actor voices Nigel, the butler who offers Stewie his crying tuxedo on Family Guy?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Da Boom," what does Meg set around Joe when she suddenly appears out of sync?

source: When Meg enters the scene to set the mouse traps around Joe, she just suddenly appears, being a few frames out of synch. This is repeated when the family walks away from New Quahog.

question: In the Family Guy episode "One if by Clam, Two if by Sea," which flag is Cleveland referencing when he says "Don't tread on me" as the guys enter the British pub?

source: Cleveland’s line “Don’t tread on me,” spoken as they enter the British pub and try to reclaim it, is a reference to the First Navy Jack ensign, which featured thirteen horizontal red lines with a rattlesnake in the foreground.

question: In the Family Guy episode "Adoptation," what does Chris do when he takes the idea to "split up" to find Tatum literally?
reply: He splits himself into two. Chris comes up with the idea to split up and look for Tatum, then takes it literally and divides his own body in half.
source: Stewie's penguin plush was found lying around, and was originally covered in blood and semen. Chris gets the idea to split up to find Tatum, but takes the idea literally and splits himself into two.

question: What was escape artist Harry Houdini's birth name?
reply: Harry Houdini's birth name was Erik Weisz. He was a Hungarian-born American magician and escapologist who lived from March 24, 1874, to October 31, 1926.
source: Harry Houdini (born Erik Weisz; March 24, 1874 – October 31, 1926) was a Hungarian-born American magician and escapologist, stunt performer, actor and film producer, as well as a skeptic and investigator of spiritualists.

question: In Family Guy, what happens to Peter when he tries to tickle Wade Boggs' cheek?
reply: Wade Boggs bites him. Boggs had been a good sport up to then and even joined the players and camp members in asking Lois to stay and play, but Peter pushed it too far by trying to tickle his cheek.
source: Being a good sport about it, Boggs joins the rest of the players and camp members in requesting that Lois stay to play. But when Peter pushes things by trying to tickle Boggs' cheek, he is bitten.

question: At the end of the Family Guy episode "Sibling Rivalry," what are Christopher Moltisanti and Stewie Griffin actually doing when they dig a hole?

question: Which actor first portrayed Dr. McCoy in the original Star Trek series?
reply: DeForest Kelley was the first to play Dr. McCoy, in the original Star Trek series. Kelley went on to play McCoy in the animated Star Trek series, seven Star Trek movies and the pilot episode of Star Trek: The Next Generation.
source: First portrayed by DeForest Kelley in the original Star Trek series, McCoy also appears in the animated Star Trek series, seven Star Trek movies, the pilot episode of Star Trek: The Next Generation, and in numerous books, comics, and video games.

question: In Family Guy, which Griffin ancestor was the only Warner Bros. animator who wanted to give Bugs Bunny a different name?

question: In the Family Guy episode "The Talented Mr. Stewie," which family member does Stewie discover previously owned his teddy bear Rupert?

question: In the Family Guy episode "Peter, Peter, Caviar Eater," which movie is referenced by the creepy twins Stewie meets?

source: The creepy twins Stewie meets are a reference to the movie version of Stephen King's "The Shining", as is Stewie's line "All work and no play makes Stewie a dull boy".

question: In the Family Guy episode "Switch the Flip," what amplifies the body-switching device so that most of the town swaps bodies?
reply: It's a fallen transformer. Brian, Chris and Peter get chased by a prostitute's pimp and smash into a power pole, and the transformer that falls boosts the device so most of the town switches bodies.
source: Brian and Chris, with Peter in tow, try to follow along to switch everyone's bodies back, but a run-in with a prostitute and her pimp that Stewie encountered earlier in Brian's body results in a car chase that ends when they smash into a power pole and a fallen transformer amplifies the device so that most of the town swaps bodies.

question: Which Osmond sister joined The Osmonds after the four founding brothers, along with Donny and Jimmy?
